name: Dama (Cameroon)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists only comparative/sociolinguistic wordlist material (Boyd 1974; Strumpell 1910; Ayotte & Ayotte 2002); no grammar or phonology

sources.citation: Strümpell, F. [with Vorbemerkungen by Bernhard Struck]. 1910. Vergleichendes Wörterverzeichnis der Heidensprachen Adamauas. Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 42: 444-488.
sources.note: Wordlist only; Dama appears as the 'Rei-Dialekt, Dama' list recorded by Lt. Dühring (p. 446). Struck's preface p. 447 remarks for the whole collection: 'Der Akzent bezeichnet in vielen Fällen.. den musikalischen Hoch- oder höheren Mittelton' (the accent mark usually denotes high or upper-mid pitch) — a transcription note, not a statement about Dama stress.

sources.citation: Elders, Stefan (ed. Roger Blench). [2012]. A wordlist of Mono, a highly endangered Adamawa language of Cameroun. ms., 25 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; Dama occurs only as the ethnonym entry gwàʔál 'Dama'. Tone-marked Mono wordlist, no phonology introduction.

sources.citation: Elders, Stefan. 2006. Issues in comparative Kebi-Benue (Adamawa). Africana Linguistica 12: 37-88.
sources.note: No stress statement. Sec. 3.4 Tone (pp. 58-59) quotes Boyd 1989a:202-203 at group level: Southern Mbum languages have two tone levels, 'the remaining subgroups have three'; adds 'The transcription of tone in Boyd's word lists has to be checked.' Dama data (glottal stop, vowel length, schwa, a- preformative) are taken from Boyd 1974; nothing on Dama accent.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2004. The Adamawa languages [classification list, 3 pp.].
sources.note: Nothing; lists Dama under Mbum > Northern > 1. Dama, 2. Ndai (Galke)/Pormi, 3. Kali.

sources.citation: Ayotte, Michael & Charlene Ayotte. 2002 [2003]. Sociolinguistic language survey of Dama, Mono, Pam, Ndai and Oblo. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-048. 12 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Purely sociolinguistic (vitality, clans, language use); sec. 3.2.1 Dama pp. 6-7. The text contains no occurrence of tone/tonal/stress/accent/phonology. CREA 126-item wordlists were collected but not published in the report.
sources.venue: Sociolinguistic language survey of Dama, Mono, Pam, Ndai and Oblo

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 reference 159004 (Ayotte & Ayotte 2002) and languoid page dama1267; SIL archive page 9104; Endangered Languages Project lang/801 (the Internet Archive 2025); Ethnologue dmm (the Internet Archive 2023); Wikipedia en/fr; Mainz Adamawa Language Projects pages
sources.note: Nothing. All cite only Ayotte & Ayotte 2002 (ELP's sole source), ALCAM 1983 and classification works; Glottolog has 0 descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) references for dama1267; Mainz project pages have no Dama material.

sources.citation: Ayotte, Michael & Charlene Ayotte. 2001-2002. Unpublished CREA 126-item wordlists of Dama, Mono, Pam, Ndai, Oblo (SIL Cameroon, Yaoundé), collected for SILESR 2002-048.

sources.note: The report says the wordlists were recorded 'to document their existence'; any tone/accent transcription of modern Dama would be there. Not published.
